editorial.headline: Temporary Accommodation, Open Nationally but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 55909 spans boarding houses, worker and student dormitories, sleeping-car operations and co-living—open nationally, but blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. Nationally, it is open to PMA and permits foreign ownership up to 100%; in Bali, however, PMA registration is blocked under the province’s island-wide, permanent rule for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. That contrast is the decisive fact for anyone considering this accommodation business: a national opening is not a Bali registration pathway.

This is a category for temporary places to stay, whether meals are provided or not and whether the arrangement uses private rooms, shared rooms or dormitory space. It includes worker dormitories, boarding houses, student accommodation provided for less than a year, sleeping cars operated independently of a railway company, and communal living, or co-living. The form can therefore include a room of one’s own, a shared room or a dormitory, with or without meals; it is defined by how temporary accommodation is supplied, not by one property type. The common thread is a stay designed for a limited period, rather than accommodation of a year or more. The category therefore accommodates several living formats, but holds them within one clear frame: temporary lodging for students, seasonal workers and other individuals.

Registration is available at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The list does not confine the activity to only one end of the business-size range. It covers the stated temporary-accommodation activity across those four scales, provided the operation remains within its defined scope. For PMA nationally, the status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In national terms, then, the ownership position is direct: foreign participation may reach the full ceiling shown for this activity.

Bali introduces a separate conclusion. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk is recorded as Low or Medium-Low on every scope, which brings the activity within the Bali moratorium. Bali’s rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration across the island, permanently; the recorded block is tied to the moratorium of May 13, 2026. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. This is not a reduction of the national 100% ceiling or a special partnership condition: it is a block on PMA registration in Bali, despite the national openness.
editorial.pullQuote: A national opening is not a Bali registration pathway when PMA registration is blocked at the provincial level.
